Making Peace with Time Alone

For when being on your own feels more like emptiness than freedom. Each day offers one small way to make time alone feel chosen, full, and kind, while keeping the door open to other people.

Loneliness · Loneliness · Self-Care · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Spend fifteen minutes alone doing something you enjoy, on purpose, and notice how it feels.
  • Day 2Write down the difference between being alone and being lonely, in your own words.
  • Day 3Take yourself somewhere nice today, a café, a park, a bookstore, and stay for a while.
  • Day 4Cook one meal for yourself as carefully as you would for a guest.
  • Day 5Write down three things you like about your own company.
  • Day 6Talk to yourself kindly out loud for a minute, the way you would to a friend who was visiting.
  • Day 7Do one thing today that you have been waiting to do "with someone." Do it alone and enjoy it.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Look back over this challenge and write down what you learned about your own company.
  • Day 60Try a new recipe from a cuisine you have never cooked, just for the fun of learning it.
  • Day 120Try a new breakfast spot alone on a weekend and sit at the counter.
  • Day 240Notice the moment tonight when you close your front door, and say "home" out loud.
  • Day 365Look back over the year and write down three ways your own company has become easier to keep.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
